synopsis: Engineering service companies can supply contracted integration, modeling and testing, while research institutes contribute methods, facilities and experienced personnel; independent assessment checks results without having built them [f16093, f16094, f16095, f16096]. Relevant off-road offerings include AVL's sector-specific validation work and tractor demonstration, Mevea's modeling and simulators, and Fraunhofer ITWM's directly relevant heavy-machinery research [f8800, f8804, f8810, f8823]. Quantitative and dated examples include AVL's claimed vehicle-model correlation of up to 97% and IDIADA's 2026 demonstration of simulated versus proving-ground automatic-braking correlation, but heavy off-road proof was not found for several other providers [f16098, f16109, f8813, f8816, f8818]. The booklet favors a hybrid arrangement: a partner accelerates the first correlated sensor model while the manufacturer retains the operating-domain definition, scenarios, acceptance criteria and correlation data [f16125]. Although the highest-cost integrated commercial tool chain can provide partner capacity for the four-month window, no public provider contract values or delivery timelines were found, and named environmental-test facilities' availability and machine-size suitability were not examined [f9313, f16126, f16124].
